propositions: Plan review must compile Round-A discovery topology into DiscoveryStagePlan units and execute through the S2 shared kernel while preserving existing YAML graph, facet packing, model ladder, concurrency limits, and cancellation semantics.

Checkpoint identity must include plan material, code/ref, criteria snapshot, prompt/contract, model/mode, topology, context, dependencies, and namespace version; any material change invalidates reuse and forces new LLM calls.

Failed, cancelled, skipped, or budget-shed work units must not serialize as clean checkpoints; earlier successes survive, independent work continues, and dependents skip per the approved final failure policy.

The review journal persists versioned safe discovery traces and success-only checkpoint envelopes separate from reducer state, while review-plan output retains only its established end-result contracts.
Shadow comparison during migration must confirm call set, order, usage, cache behavior, and verdict are identical between legacy and new paths with zero duplicate LLM calls.
Legacy and corrupt checkpoint envelopes must produce zero reuse and trigger fresh execution rather than checkpoint restoration.
